lead: A neighbourhood of blocks and working families, between Montjuïc, the Zona Franca and L'Hospitalet.
text: Until the 20th century it was farmland, with farmhouses such as Can Mestres. As the Zona Franca industrial estate grew, residents arrived from many regions of Spain, and the present neighbourhood, with its densely populated streets, was born of that wave: 31,768 inhabitants in 1.27 km². Its origin is tied to the castle of Port and its chapel, from the late 10th century. In February 2025 the Can Clos park opened, with 24,700 m² landscaped, 14,400 of them gardens, and the special neighbourhood plan (Pla de Barris) for La Marina adds 50 million euros of public investment until 2028.

Its average rent, 885 €/month, is the lowest in Sants-Montjuïc, and its sale price, 2,936 €/m², is also among the lowest in the district. For anyone looking for a first home, it is a neighbourhood to consider, with good connections to Montjuïc and Gran Via. If you are selling, the average sale price is 24% below the Sants-Montjuïc average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 235,000 € on average, and this is one of the most affordable neighbourhoods in Sants-Montjuïc (7th of 8 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 12% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of flats on densely populated streets, with a farmhouse here and there recalling the farming past.
